title: Lifecycle Controls: Prompt/Response TTLs, Residency Rules, and Evidence Automation SDK
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design and deliver a unified, developer-first mechanism (UI + API + SDK) that lets tenants define precise lifecycle controls for interactive artifacts: prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics. Controls must express TTLs, conditional sampling, regional residency constraints, and automated evidence bundling for audits. This work bridges policy authoring, enforcement in the serving runtime, and attestable export paths for legal/compliance teams.

Goals: 
- Provide expressive yet composable retention rules (per-tenant, per-route, per-model) that can express: fixed TTLs, event-driven TTLs (e.g., on user deletion), sampled retention (retain N% or stratified by label), and legal-hold overrides.
- Enforce residency: allow rules scoped by geography (region, country, cloud region) and prevent cross-region retention unless explicitly permitted.
- Build an Evidence Automation SDK that can generate signed, timestamped bundles containing artefacts (prompts, responses, logs, metrics snapshots) and provenance metadata for exports. Bundles must include hash chains and an access manifest for auditors.
- Expose a Preview & Simulator in Console to let customers estimate storage and sampling outcomes before applying changes.
- Integrate enforcement with serving/runtime so policy decisions are evaluated at ingress and in async pipelines (archival/export).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) API: new /retention-rules endpoints for CRUD of retention policies, with JSON schema supporting conditions (route, model, tag), actions (delete, archive, export), TTL expressions, and residency constraints. Documented in OpenAPI and SDKs.
2) Console UX: a guided flow (rules wizard) to create per-route TTLs and regional constraints, plus a simulator that shows expected percent of retained artifacts and estimated storage/cost impact.
3) Evidence SDK: versioned Python + TypeScript packages able to request snapshots, assemble a signed evidence bundle, and push to customer-configured S3/GCS or trigger secure transfer. Bundles include cryptographic hashes (SHA-256), manifest.json, and chain-of-custody metadata.
4) Runtime enforcement: rules are compiled to a policy graph consumed by runtime and async archivers. For each request, the runtime emits an evaluation result and storage directive. Directives are visible in request logs.
5) Auditability: exports are discoverable in Console with signed attestations and export timestamps. Automated reports for legal holds and deletion operations.
6) Migration: provide a one-click preview and migration planner for existing tenants using default/global TTL to adopt new scoped policies.

Proposed design notes: 
- Rule model: adopt a small DSL: {scope, conditions[], ttl:ISO8601 | "forever" | "on_event:USER_DELETE", sampling:{type:"ratio"|"stratified", value:0.05}, residency:{allowed_regions:[], deny_cross_region:true}, action:{type:"delete"|"archive"|"export", export_config_id}}. The DSL is validated server-side.
- Evaluation point: keep decision fast by compiling rules into prefix trees keyed by (tenant, route, model). At runtime this should be an O(log n) lookup.
- Sampling: implement deterministic sampling via tenant-scoped consistent hashing to ensure reproducibility across distributed workers.
- Evidence bundle format: tar.gz with manifest.json, one-line sorted SHA-256 index, and a signature file (ed25519) produced by the customer's KMS or Redwood signing service (opt-in).
- Residency enforcement: two enforcement layers: soft (warning + simulation) for admin preview, then strict (deny archive/export to disallowed regions) when enabled.

Trade-offs & risks: 
- Complex DSL increases cognitive load for PMs; mitigate with templates and presets (e.g., GDPR-short, PCI-long, Low-Retention-Mode).
- Sampling can complicate forensic audits; we will include mapping keys and sampling seeds in bundles to allow reconstruction of sampling decisions.
- Runtime lookups add latency; we plan a local cache with 1s TTL and metrics to track policy cache misses.

Implementation plan (high level): 
1) Design: schema + initial SDK surface + console wireframes. (Owners: PM/Design) 
2) API & schema: OpenAPI, backend endpoints, validation. (Owners: Backend Eng) 
3) Runtime hooks: compile rules into runtime config, add evaluation path at request acceptance and async archiver. (Owners: Serving Runtime Eng) 
4) Evidence SDK: draft Python + TS packages, sign support, sample integrator. (Owners: Developer DX) 
5) Console: wizard + simulator + export browser. (Owners: Console UX) 
6) E2E tests, security review, and staged rollout behind feature flag. (Owners: QA/Sec/Eng)

Telemetry & success metrics: 
- Number of tenants with scoped retention rules enabled.
- % of exported bundles that include signatures (attestation adoption).
- Reduction in average retained bytes per request for customers adopting sampling presets.
- Audit run-time: time from request to evidence bundle generation.

Dependencies: 
- ENG-51234 (runtime configurator for policy-based retention) for integration hooks.
- ENG-22456 (deterministic purge orchestrator) for deletion workflows.
- Design input for wizard (DES-59218) for compact console flows.

Open questions: 
- Should evidence bundles support encryption at rest using tenant-managed KMS keys by default? (security input required)
- How to represent legal-hold overrides that apply retroactively without violating deletion guarantees? Proposed: maintain a separate legal-hold index that prevents purge and triggers re-ingestion to long-term archive.
- Cross-tenant sampling policy: allow org-wide presets vs per-team overrides — need product discussion.

References & artifacts: 
- Draft OpenAPI: https://confluence.internal/redwood/retention-openapi (WIP)
- Draft wireframes: https://drive.google.com/designs/retention-wizard-v1
- Evidence bundle spec (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-evidence-spec
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-51234, ENG-22456

Rollout plan: 
- Alpha: internal Redwood tenants + small set of early access customers (feature-flagged).
- Beta: enable console wizard + SDK, collect feedback and iterate.
- GA: enable templates, signed bundles, and residency enforcement by default for new tenants.

Privacy/regulatory notes: align templates to GDPR/CCPA/PCI where applicable. For EU-only tenants, residency default = deny_cross_region true.

Acceptance tester checklist: 
- Create a per-route rule with TTL=7d, verify requests older than 7 days are purged by orchestrator.
- Create sampled rule (10%) and demonstrate deterministic sample selection and bundle mapping.
- Create residency-deny rule and attempt export to disallowed region; verify rejection and audit log.
- Generate evidence bundle and verify signature/manifest integrity with provided tooling.
